title: AWS Announces General Availability of DevOps Agent for Automated Incident Investigation
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/aws-devops-agent-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775576531730.jpg"/><p>AWS has announced the general availability of DevOps Agent, a generative AI–powered assistant designed to help developers and operators troubleshoot issues, analyze deployments, and automate operational tasks across AWS environments.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Pulumi Adds Full Bun Runtime Support
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/pulumi-bun-support/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1776413456207.jpg"/><p>Pulumi has announced that Bun is now a fully supported runtime for Pulumi, going beyond its previous role as merely a package manager option. With the new release of Pulumi 3.227.0, developers can set runtime: bun in their Pulumi.yaml and have Bun execute their entire infrastructure program, with no Node.js installation required.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: CNCF Warns Kubernetes Alone Is Not Enough to Secure LLM Workloads
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/kubernetes-secure-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775830657737.jpg"/><p>A new blog from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation highlights a critical gap in how organizations are deploying large language models (LLMs) on Kubernetes: while Kubernetes excels at orchestrating and isolating workloads, it does not inherently understand or control the behavior of AI systems, creating a fundamentally different and more complex threat model.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: AWS Launches Agent Registry in Preview to Govern AI Agent Sprawl Across Enterprises
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/aws-agent-registry-preview/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1776064171956.jpg"/><p>AWS released Agent Registry in preview as part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, providing a centralized catalog for discovering, governing, and reusing AI agents, tools, and MCP servers across organizations. The registry indexes agents regardless of where they run and supports both MCP and A2A protocols natively. Microsoft, Google Cloud, and the ACP Registry offer competing solutions.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: AWS Introduces S3 Files, Bringing File System Access to S3 Buckets
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/aws-s3-files/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1776284137747.jpg"/><p>AWS recently introduced S3 Files, which lets users mount an Amazon S3 bucket and access its data through a standard file system interface. Applications can read and write files using standard file operations, while the system automatically translates them into S3 requests, allowing compute services to work directly with data stored in S3.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Presentation: From VR to Flat Screens: Bridging the Input and Immersion Gap
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/game-vr-flat-screens/en/mediumimage/medium-1775637585504.jpg"/><p>Dany Lepage discusses the architectural journey of porting a hit VR title to seven non-VR platforms. He explains how his team solved the challenges of cross-progression, diverse input paradigms, and maintaining release velocity across Steam, iOS, and PlayStation. Beyond the tech, he shares candid lessons on the "product fit" gap when translating immersive social presence to 2D screens.</p> <i>By Dany Lepage</i>

title: OpenTelemetry Declarative Configuration Reaches Stability Milestone
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/opentelemetry-declarative-config/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1776292543355.jpg"/><p>The OpenTelemetry project has announced that key portions of its declarative configuration specification have reached stable status. The observability framework is a vendor-neutral and language-agnostic way to configure telemetry collection.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Article: Using AWS Lambda Extensions to Run Post-Response Telemetry Flush
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/lambda-extension-deferred-flush/en/headerimage/lambda-extension-deferred-flush-header-1775648097720.jpg"/><p>At Lead Bank, synchronous telemetry flushing caused intermittent exporter stalls to become user-facing 504 gateway timeouts. By leveraging AWS Lambda's Extensions API and goroutine chaining in Go, flush work is moved off the response path, returning responses immediately while preserving full observability without telemetry loss.</p> <i>By Melvin Philips</i>

title: New Rowhammer Attacks on NVIDIA GPUs Enable Full System Takeover
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/rowhammer-attacks-nvidia/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775830147456.jpg"/><p>Security researchers have demonstrated a new class of Rowhammer attacks targeting NVIDIA GPUs that can escalate from memory corruption to full system compromise, marking a significant shift in hardware-level security risks.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: Platform Engineering: Lessons from the Rise and Fall of eBay Velocity
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/platform-engineering-lessons/en/mediumimage/randy-shoup-medium-1775637120944.jpg"/><p>Randy Shoup discusses the "Velocity Initiative," a transformation that doubled engineering productivity and modernized eBay’s DORA metrics. He shares the technical playbook used to scale 4,500 services while explaining why even elite engineering execution can’t save a company hampered by waterfall planning, risk aversion, and a "pathological" culture of fear.</p> <i>By Randy Shoup</i>

title: Article: Beyond One-Click: Designing an Enterprise-Grade Observability Extension for Docker
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/enterprise-grade-observability-extension-docker/en/headerimage/enterprise-grade-observability-extension-docker-header-1775560652994.jpg"/><p>Docker Extensions boost developer speed but create a "visibility gap" by isolating telemetry. To meet enterprise needs, extensions must act as bridges to centralized platforms. This article details how to use OpenTelemetry, policy-as-code, and encryption to build secure pipelines. Learn to balance developer productivity with the governance required for scalable, compliant observability.</p> <i>By Pragya Keshap</i>

title: Airbnb Migrates High-Volume Metrics Pipeline to OpenTelemetry
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/airbnd-opentelemetry-vmagent/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1776092205754.jpg"/><p>Airbnb's observability engineering team has published details of a large-scale migration away from StatsD and a proprietary Veneur-based aggregation pipeline toward a modern, open-source metrics stack built on OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP), the OpenTelemetry Collector, and VictoriaMetrics' vmagent. The resulting system now ingests over 100 million samples per second in production.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Podcast: How SBOMs and Engineering Discipline Can Help You Avoid Trivy’s Compromise
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/help-avoid-trivy-compromise/en/smallimage/the-infoq-podcast-logo-thumbnail-1775549272964.jpg"/><p>Viktor Peterson, part of the CISA task force working on SBOM blueprints and co-founder of sbomify, explores the shifting landscape of software supply chain security as the EU's Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) comes into force, a "GDPR moment" for the industry.</p> <i>By Viktor Peterson</i>

title: AWS Launches Sustainability Console with API Access and Scope 1-3 Emissions Reporting
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS launched a standalone Sustainability console with API access, configurable CSV exports, and Scope 1-3 emissions data by service and Region. The console decouples emissions reporting from billing permissions. AWS CTO Werner Vogels framed carbon as an architectural metric belonging alongside latency, cost, and error rates in the observability stack.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: GitHub Copilot CLI Reaches General Availability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/github-copilot-cli-ga/en/headerimage/header-1775595985599.jpeg"/><p>GitHub has launched Copilot CLI into general availability, bringing generative AI directly to the terminal. Integrated with the GitHub CLI, it offers natural language command suggestions and code explanations. Recent updates introduce "agentic" workflows with Autopilot mode and GPT-5.4 support, alongside new enterprise telemetry for tracking usage across development teams.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>
